sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `cursor`
- Canonical name: Cursor (`claim-cursor-sf-identity`; existing canonical `claim-cursor-identity` is not reused)
- Current status: actively shipped commercial product (`claim-cursor-sf-status`, `claim-cursor-sf-maintenance`, `claim-cursor-sf-maintenance-changelog`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-15
- Canonical URL: https://cursor.com/ (`claim-cursor-sf-canonical-url`)
- Vendor strings in first-party sources conflict: Anysphere, Inc. on the Terms of Service (`claim-cursor-sf-vendor-anysphere`) and a 2026-08-14 post stating Cursor was acquired by SpaceX (`claim-cursor-sf-vendor-spacex`)
- Desktop latest labeled 3.16 (`claim-cursor-sf-version-2026-08-15`). A 2026-08-14 observation recorded 3.15 as Latest (`claim-cursor-sf-version`)
- Public product repository: unknown (`claim-cursor-sf-repository-url`)

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: a coding agent and AI editor that official pages also present as one agent across desktop, CLI, integrations, web, and mobile (`claim-cursor-sf-what-it-is`, `claim-cursor-sf-what-it-is-product`)
- What it is not: the iOS app is not an IDE, admin console, editor, terminal, or file browser (`claim-cursor-sf-not-mobile-ide`). A native Android app is planned (`claim-cursor-sf-not-android-native`); Android users are sent to a Chrome PWA (`claim-cursor-sf-surface-android-pwa`)

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `ide` (`claim-cursor-sf-primary-type`)
- Secondary role: `cloud-agent` (`claim-cursor-sf-secondary-role-cloud-agent`)
- Agent-loop owner: Cursor Agent owns instructions/rules, tools, and per-model orchestration (`claim-cursor-sf-agent-loop`)
- Architecture: the TypeScript SDK says the same agent runs in the Cursor IDE, CLI, and web app and is scriptable from TypeScript (`claim-cursor-sf-architecture`). JetBrains ACP is a separate integration (`claim-cursor-sf-surface-jetbrains`). Agents Window is a separate desktop interface claim (`claim-cursor-sf-surface-agents-window`)

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-cursor-desktop-ide`, `surface-cursor-cli`, `surface-cursor-web-agents`, `surface-cursor-ios`, `surface-cursor-android-pwa`, `surface-cursor-slack`, `surface-cursor-microsoft-teams`, `surface-cursor-jetbrains-acp`, `surface-cursor-sdk`, `surface-cursor-remote-control-client`, `surface-cursor-remote-control-relay`, `surface-cursor-desktop-ssh`, `surface-cursor-github-dispatch`, `surface-cursor-github-scm`, `surface-cursor-bitbucket-dispatch`, `surface-cursor-bitbucket-scm`, `surface-cursor-private-network`, `surface-cursor-linear-dispatch`, `surface-cursor-jira-dispatch`, `surface-cursor-notion-dispatch`, `surface-cursor-self-hosted-pool`, `surface-cursor-my-machines`, `surface-cursor-cloud-remote-desktop`, `surface-cursor-gitlab-scm`, `surface-cursor-azure-devops-scm`
- Execution location: same-device for desktop Agent tools (`claim-cursor-sf-execution-local`); same-device terminal for CLI tools (`claim-cursor-sf-execution-cli`); isolated vendor-cloud VMs for Cloud Agents (`claim-cursor-sf-execution-cloud`); Remote Control keeps tools on the user's computer while the loop runs in Cursor cloud (`claim-cursor-sf-execution-remote-control`); Self-Hosted Pool and My Machines execute tools on user-controlled hosts (`claim-cursor-sf-surface-self-hosted-pool`, `claim-cursor-sf-surface-my-machines`)

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: selectable multi-provider catalog, Auto modes, and Cursor Router; SDK local mode still uses hosted inference (`claim-cursor-sf-model-strategy`, `claim-cursor-sf-models-hosted`)
- Auth strategy: Terms require an account for most features (`claim-cursor-sf-auth-account`); pricing lists Teams SSO and Enterprise SCIM (`claim-cursor-sf-auth-strategy`); optional BYOK still routes through Cursor's backend (`claim-cursor-sf-byok`)
- Provider support: hosted catalog providers on Models & Pricing are Cursor, SpaceXAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google (`claim-cursor-sf-provider-support`). BYOK Azure OpenAI and AWS Bedrock are on the API-keys page (`claim-cursor-sf-provider-support-byok`)
- First-party local-model runtime: unknown (`claim-cursor-sf-models-hosted`)

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: per-model default and max windows on the docs homepage (`claim-cursor-sf-context`). Interactive Cloud Agents can select window size (`claim-cursor-sf-context-cloud-select`). Automations use the model maximum with no toggle (`claim-cursor-sf-context-automations-max`). iOS runs use the model maximum (`claim-cursor-sf-context-ios-max`)
- Memory: rules and `AGENTS.md` are prompt-level persistence because models do not retain memory between completions (`claim-cursor-sf-memory-rules`). Automations can keep Memories across runs (`claim-cursor-sf-memory-automations`)
- Compaction: CLI `/summarize` (`/compress` alias) (`claim-cursor-sf-compaction`); hooks `preCompact` (`claim-cursor-sf-compaction-precompact`)
- Session behavior: desktop checkpoints and queues (`claim-cursor-sf-session`); CLI resume/worktrees (`claim-cursor-sf-session-cli`); cross-device cloud handoff (`claim-cursor-sf-session-cross-device`)

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: search, web, rules fetch, file read/edit, shell, browser, image generation, clarifying questions (`claim-cursor-sf-tools`)
- Extensions: plugins and marketplace bundles (`claim-cursor-sf-extensions`)
- MCP: stdio, SSE, and Streamable HTTP client (`claim-cursor-sf-mcp`). Xcode 26.3+ exposes built-in MCP tools through `xcrun mcpbridge` (`claim-cursor-sf-xcode-mcp`)
- Skills: Agent Skills plus built-in Cursor skills (`claim-cursor-sf-skills`)
- Hooks: project, user, team, and enterprise hook scripts (`claim-cursor-sf-hooks`)
- APIs: TypeScript SDK, Cloud Agents REST API, and SDK Bridge (`claim-cursor-sf-api`); Python SDK (`claim-cursor-sf-api-python`)

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: parent agent delegates to built-in or custom subagents, including nested and cloud subagents (`claim-cursor-sf-orchestration`)
- Parallelism: parallel local subagents and cloud subagents (`claim-cursor-sf-parallelism`); Agents Window many parallel cloud agents (`claim-cursor-sf-parallelism-agents-window`)

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: local OS sandbox on macOS/Linux via Run Modes (`claim-cursor-sf-isolation-local`); product page says sandboxed by default (`claim-cursor-sf-sandbox-marketing`); CLI sandbox is a toggle (`claim-cursor-sf-sandbox-cli`); Cloud Agents use isolated AWS VMs and auto-run commands (`claim-cursor-sf-isolation-cloud`); Cloud Agents do not use desktop Run Modes (`claim-cursor-sf-isolation-cloud-no-run-modes`)
- Permissions: default approval for sensitive actions and terminal commands; the security page names Run Modes as allowlist through Auto-review (`claim-cursor-sf-permissions`). The three named modes Auto-review, Allowlist, and Run Everything are on the Run Modes page (`claim-cursor-sf-permissions-run-modes`)
- Security: SOC 2 Type II, annual pen tests, and Privacy Mode on the security page (`claim-cursor-sf-security`); Enterprise pricing lists audit logs (`claim-cursor-sf-tag-audit-trail`); Cloud Agent outbound allowlists are on Secrets & Network (`claim-cursor-sf-security-cloud-allowlists`)
- Data path: Privacy Mode blocks training; indexing uploads chunks; all requests including BYOK pass through Cursor's backend; Cloud Agents need non-legacy Privacy Mode (`claim-cursor-sf-data-path`)

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: marketing page and docs conflict on Individual Pro+/Ultra dollar amounts (`claim-cursor-sf-pricing-page`, `claim-cursor-sf-pricing-docs`)
- License: proprietary commercial Terms of Service (`claim-cursor-sf-license`)
- Maintenance: desktop latest 3.16 on downloads as of 2026-08-15 (`claim-cursor-sf-maintenance-2026-08-15`, `claim-cursor-sf-version-2026-08-15`); a 2026-08-14 observation recorded 3.15 as Latest (`claim-cursor-sf-maintenance`, `claim-cursor-sf-version`); changelog through 2026-08-13 (`claim-cursor-sf-maintenance-changelog`)
- Lock-in: subscriptions only via cursor.com (`claim-cursor-sf-lock-in`); BYOK still uses Cursor's backend (`claim-cursor-sf-byok`)
- Availability: desktop macOS/Windows/Linux (`claim-cursor-sf-availability`); CLI (`claim-cursor-sf-availability-cli`); iOS beta (`claim-cursor-sf-availability-ios`). iOS plan lists conflict (`claim-cursor-sf-ios-plans-include-start`, `claim-cursor-sf-ios-plans-omit-start`, `claim-cursor-sf-start-includes-cloud-ios`)

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: classic editor is described as the IDE with VS Code extensions; this is not an official `fork_of` claim (`claim-cursor-sf-lineage-vscode`)
- Compatibility: Cursor reads `.claude` and `.codex` skills directories (`claim-cursor-sf-compatibility-skills`) and `.claude`/`.codex` agents directories (`claim-cursor-sf-compatibility-subagents`)
- Relationship edges: none restaged. Canonical inbound edges already exist (`conductor --orchestrates--> cursor`, `t3-code --wraps_cli--> cursor`) and were not copied. No first-party Cursor-owned outbound edge to another project id was established.

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: vendor positioning as one agent across Desktop, CLI, GitHub, Slack, Linear, JetBrains, web, and mobile (`claim-cursor-sf-unique`)
- Meaningful drawbacks: Auto-review is not a hard security boundary (`claim-cursor-sf-drawback`); cloud-storage gates for Cloud Agents and Remote Control (`claim-cursor-sf-drawback-cloud-storage`); mobile client is not an IDE (`claim-cursor-sf-not-mobile-ide`); purchase lock-in (`claim-cursor-sf-lock-in`); BYOK still uses Cursor's backend (`claim-cursor-sf-byok`)
- Best fit: documented audiences are individual developers, teams, and enterprises (`claim-cursor-sf-intended-user`). This is not a recommendation.
- Not-for: Start exclusions (`claim-cursor-sf-not-for`); Hobby limits (`claim-cursor-sf-not-for-hobby`); Cloud Agents require a paid plan (`claim-cursor-sf-cloud-needs-paid-plan`); iOS is not an IDE (`claim-cursor-sf-not-mobile-ide`)
